short: Effects of combined surface treatments of aluminium nanopart
title: Effects of combined surface treatments of aluminium nanoparticle on its corrosion resistance before and after inclusion into an epoxy coating

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Al nanoparticle fillers for anticorrosive epoxy coatings on steel corrode themselves and aggregate in the resin. Ce and/or amino-silane surface layers on Al nanoparticles should inhibit their corrosion and improve coating protection.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/need), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/modification), n4 (DES/variable_sweep), n5 (PRC/deposition), n6 (PRC/synthesis), n7 (PRC/deposition)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Ce layer is very thin and non-uniform; nanoparticles are only partly covered by Ce oxides/hydroxides. Amino-silane is chemically grafted on the nanoparticles; Si-Al-2 and Si-Ce-Al carry the most silane.
states.detail: Absorbed: n9 (STR/microstructure/distribution), n10 (STR/chemistry/bonding), n13 (STR/microstructure/distribution). Premises: O 1s components: CeO2 ~529.1, Ce2O3 ~530.0, Al-O ~531.0, Ce-OH ~532.0 eV; TGA stage III (250-425 C) mass loss of silanised particles is decomposition of chemically grafted aminosilane

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Silanisation turns the particle surface from polar to non-polar; Ce-treated particles stay polar like bare Al. Surface layers lower H2 evolution of Al nanoparticles in pH 1 acid; Si-Al-2 lowest after 15 h, Ce-Al/pH 3.8 lowest up to ~6 h.
states.detail: Absorbed: n11 (PRP/value), n12 (PRP/value), n14 (MEC/pathway), n15 (MEC/pathway), n16 (PRP/value), n19 (PRP/value). Premises: Smaller NTU change over 60 min means a more stable dispersion in the solvent; MEK has a higher polar solubility parameter than butyl acetate; non-polar and H-bond parameters similar; Terminal NH2 groups of aminosilanes react with epoxide groups of the resin; One capacitive time constant with phase near 90 deg means an intact barrier; two time constants signal delamination onset

states.title: Performance state
states.head: After 360 h salt spray the steel under S2 (and S4) coatings is almost uncorroded, while the blank is fully corroded

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: APTES treatment (best Si-Al-2 at 2 wt%) gives dispersed, barrier-enhancing Al fillers; Ce film protects bare particles but aggregates in epoxy and adds little

nodes.title: ASSAY, EDS:spectrum, F1
nodes.head: EDS Ce content rises from 0.5 to 1.1% between pH 3.0 and 3.8, then drops to 0.9% at pH 4.2
nodes.note: Al ~82-83%, O ~14%, N 2-2.7% at all pH; in F1a the labelled Ce L lines (4.8-6 keV) show no visible peak above background
nodes.detail: o1: EDS Ce content rises from 0.5 to 1.1% between pH 3.0 and 3.8, then drops to 0.9% at pH 4.2
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n6 (o1).

nodes.title: SEM, F3
nodes.head: Al and Ce-Al particles look the same: smooth agglomerated spheres, no visible surface layer
nodes.solves: Ce layer is very thin and non-uniform; nanoparticles are only partly covered by Ce oxides/hydroxides
nodes.note: annotated diameters 75-153 nm (a) and 51-134 nm (b); a very thin layer below SEM resolution cannot be excluded or shown
nodes.necessity_reason: n9 keeps shown support from o3, o5, o20, o21 after removal.

nodes.title: MICRO, F8
nodes.head: Un3 particles pile in one dense cluster; S3 particles sit in several smaller groups across the fracture surface
nodes.solves: Silane-modified nanoparticles are better dispersed in the epoxy than unmodified ones
nodes.note: S3 particles are still clustered, not individually dispersed; one field per sample
nodes.necessity_reason: No member reaches image_support shown and n13 has no other figure-backed support.

nodes.title: evidence, F2
nodes.head: O 1s envelope fitted with CeO2, Ce2O3, Al-O and Ce-OH components; Al-O is the largest. Ce 3d inset shows only noise-level ripples; no distinct Ce 3d doublet above background.
nodes.solves: Ce layer is very thin and non-uniform; nanoparticles are only partly covered by Ce oxides/hydroxides
nodes.op: assign features, compare with reference value, cross check consistency
nodes.note: Ce2O3 component is labelled 'Ce2O' on the figure linked text lists Ce 3d among the main survey peaks metal at higher BE than oxide and metal-dominated surface are inconsistent with reference values; suggests a charging shift or mis-assignment affecting all BE assignments text: Ce oxides much less intense than hydroxides, order Ce-OH < Ce2O3 < CeO2; figure shows the reverse for peak heights
nodes.detail: o3: O 1s envelope fitted with CeO2, Ce2O3, Al-O and Ce-OH components; Al-O is the largest; o5: Ce 3d inset shows only noise-level ripples; no distinct Ce 3d doublet above background; o20: Al 2p fit labels Al2O3 at ~75.4 eV and a ~4x larger Al metal peak at ~78.2 eV, above the oxide; o21: O 1s: Ce2O3 component (~275) is taller than Ce-OH (~250); CeO2 is smallest (~100)
nodes.inner_audit: o5: linked text lists Ce 3d among the main survey peaks; o20: metal at higher BE than oxide and metal-dominated surface are inconsistent with reference values; suggests a charging shift or mis-assignment affecting all BE assignments

nodes.title: evidence, F4
nodes.head: Final mass retention at 425 C: Si-Al-2 ~95.3% < Si-Ce-Al ~95.9% ~ Si-Al-1 ~96.0% < Si-Al-3 ~97.5% < Al ~99.5%
nodes.solves: Amino-silane is chemically grafted on the nanoparticles; Si-Al-2 and Si-Ce-Al carry the most silane
nodes.note: largest drops in stage III for Si-Al-1 and Si-Al-2; Al curve rises after ~375 C; packet F4 is paper Fig. 5
nodes.detail: o6: Final mass retention at 425 C: Si-Al-2 ~95.3% < Si-Ce-Al ~95.9% ~ Si-Al-1 ~96.0% < Si-Al-3 ~97.5% < Al ~99.5%
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n10 (o6).

nodes.title: ASSAY, F5, F6
nodes.head: In MEK, bare Al keeps the highest turbidity (3750 to 1260 NTU); all silanised samples stay far lower; Ce-Al pH 3.4-4.2 track Al. In butyl acetate, Si-Al-1, Si-Al-2 and Si-Ce-Al stay above bare Al; Si-Al-3 ends near Al (~500 NTU)
nodes.solves: Silanisation turns the particle surface from polar to non-polar; Ce-treated particles stay polar like bare Al
nodes.note: Ce-Al/pH 3.0 falls lowest in F6a (2800 to 720 NTU); silanised samples start at 1450-2000 NTU all curves fall by 60-70% over 60 min; silanised 850-1050 vs Al ~500 NTU at 60 min
nodes.detail: o7: In MEK, bare Al keeps the highest turbidity (3750 to 1260 NTU); all silanised samples stay far lower; Ce-Al pH 3.4-4.2 track Al; o8: In butyl acetate, Si-Al-1, Si-Al-2 and Si-Ce-Al stay above bare Al; Si-Al-3 ends near Al (~500 NTU)
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n11 (o7, o8).

nodes.title: ASSAY, F7
nodes.head: H2 volume after 900 min: Al 1.7 mL highest; Si-Al-2 0.7, Si-Ce-Al 0.9, Si-Al-1 1.0, Ce-Al 1.2-1.5, Si-Al-3 1.6. Silanised samples already show 0.1-0.2 mL H2 at 90-190 min, like bare Al; no 140-min gas-free period is visible
nodes.solves: Surface layers lower H2 evolution of Al nanoparticles in pH 1 acid; Si-Al-2 lowest after 15 h, Ce-Al/pH 3.8 lowest up to ~6 h
nodes.op: compare across conditions, read characteristic point
nodes.note: F7c: Ce-Al/pH 3.8 lowest until ~390 min, then overtakes Si-Al-2 and Si-Ce-Al linked text: no hydrogen evolved during the first 140 min for silanised samples, latency far beyond unmodified
nodes.detail: o9: H2 volume after 900 min: Al 1.7 mL highest; Si-Al-2 0.7, Si-Ce-Al 0.9, Si-Al-1 1.0, Ce-Al 1.2-1.5, Si-Al-3 1.6; o10: Silanised samples already show 0.1-0.2 mL H2 at 90-190 min, like bare Al; no 140-min gas-free period is visible
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n12 (o9, o10).

nodes.title: PHYS:porosity, F8
nodes.head: S3 fracture surface shows several round cavities ~200-500 nm wide
nodes.solves: Well-dispersed, passivated particles cut coating free volume and porosity, lowering electrolyte permeation (barrier effect)
nodes.note: text never mentions them; could be pull-out sockets or voids, bearing on the low-porosity barrier claim; judge: Un3 (F8a) also shows one round cavity (~230 nm), so cavities are not unique to S3; S3 cavities ~290-460 nm by the 2.89 um view field
nodes.detail: o22: S3 fracture surface shows several round cavities ~200-500 nm wide
nodes.inner_audit: o22: text never mentions them; could be pull-out sockets or voids, bearing on the low-porosity barrier claim; judge: Un3 (F8a) also shows one round cavity (~230 nm), so cavities are not unique to S3; S3 cavities ~290-460 nm by the 2.89 um view field

nodes.title: evidence, F10
nodes.head: S2 and S4 reach log|Z| ~10.5 at 0.01 Hz with phase ~90 deg over most frequencies; S3 ~6.9; blank ~4.5. log|Z| at 0.01 Hz: M2 7.0 > M3 5.9 > M1 4.9; Un2 5.4 > Un1 4.7 > blank 4.5 > Un3 4.2
nodes.solves: Low-frequency impedance after 57 d in 3.5% NaCl ranks S2/S4 (~1e10 ohm cm2) >> M2 (~1e7) > Un and blank (~1e4-1e5)
nodes.note: S1 |Z| series is hidden behind S2/S4 markers; S3 phase stays low (~10 deg) below 10 Hz Ce-Al ranking is non-monotonic in loading (M3 < M2), against the linked-text statement that protection rises with Ce-Al concentration
nodes.detail: o12: S2 and S4 reach log|Z| ~10.5 at 0.01 Hz with phase ~90 deg over most frequencies; S3 ~6.9; blank ~4.5; o13: log|Z| at 0.01 Hz: M2 7.0 > M3 5.9 > M1 4.9; Un2 5.4 > Un1 4.7 > blank 4.5 > Un3 4.2
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n16 (o12, o13).

nodes.title: evidence, F11, F12
nodes.head: Adhesion loss: blank ~44%; Un 34-38%; M 23-29%; S 18-25%, lowest S4 ~18% and S2 ~18.5%. After pull-off, dry S2 dolly area is fully covered; wet S2 shows only a small bare-steel patch vs a fully bare wet blank
nodes.solves: Pull-off strength loss after salt spray is lowest for silane-modified filler coatings (~18%) and highest for the blank (~44%)
nodes.note: error bars of Un1 and Un3 span ~10-17 points; S3 has the largest S error bar dry S3 and S4 show large bare-steel areas (adhesive failure); M3 dry similar in the whole F11
nodes.detail: o18: Adhesion loss: blank ~44%; Un 34-38%; M 23-29%; S 18-25%, lowest S4 ~18% and S2 ~18.5%; o19: After pull-off, dry S2 dolly area is fully covered; wet S2 shows only a small bare-steel patch vs a fully bare wet blank
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n19 (o18, o19).

nodes.title: ASSAY:stain, F9
nodes.head: Under S2 the steel is bright with rust only along the scribe; M2 lightly stained; M1, M3 and blank widely rusted
nodes.solves: After 360 h salt spray the steel under S2 (and S4) coatings is almost uncorroded, while the blank is fully corroded
nodes.note: S4 rust along scribe with slight spreading; S1 speckled; S3 a localized blister-like rust patch; Un series (F9a) widely rusted except half of Un2
